page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server optimized for high-performance computing workloads. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz, featuring 48 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core configuration. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 150 Gbps, while local storage is absent, requiring external network-attached storage solutions.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The server achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is a key strength, with large-block read-only and write operations both ranking in the top 10%, reaching 695.05 GB/sec and 347.3 GB/sec respectively. Single-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, while software compilation with Clang and PassMark physics tests also demonstrate top-tier execution speeds.

From a resource density perspective, the hpc7a.24xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for parallel computing tasks that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading overhead. The 1:16 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides substantial memory capacity per core, reducing memory bottlenecks in large-scale simulations. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents a clear tradeoff, making this instance less suitable for local-storage-heavy database operations or GPU-accelerated deep learning workloads.

This instance is highly suited for compute-intensive and memory-bandwidth-bound workloads. Appropriate use cases include high-performance computing simulations, molecular modeling, computational fluid dynamics, software compilation, and parallel data processing. It is also well-suited for high-throughput Redis operations and memory-intensive scientific computing.
